summary: Delivered the first production non-fork Rust/OXC lint slice. A compact native overlay recognizes representative @{ and @if/@else outside protected lexical regions, makes one equal-width TSRX-only projection, and drives one canonical OXC parser/semantic/linter pass at exact original UTF-8 byte spans. Real no-debugger/no-unused-vars diagnostics, an identity-proven OXC no-var fix with validation reparse, an in-memory library boundary, and a zero-scan ordinary-TSX bypass are retained in black-box and unit tests. Release P01/P02/P03/P05/P07 gates pass with raw samples; no OXC source is copied, forked, vendored, patched, or imported outside crates/oxc_adapter.

architecture_invariants: The sole revision-specific OXC dependency/API boundary is crates/oxc_adapter.
Ordinary source enters canonical OXC directly with no scan or projection allocation.
Non-fix TSRX lint performs one full OXC parse; fix validation performs one explicit post-edit reparse.
No compiled-TSX second parse, source map, AST conversion, JSON/JS AST, per-node heap graph, OXC source copy, Cargo patch, or local OXC checkout exists.
Markless and every external repository remained read-only.
limitations: Grammar is intentionally limited to representative @{, @if, and @else; templates are currently opaque and regex/complete JSX lexical edge cases remain future work.
The performance corpus models the supported Markless-style subset and does not prove the complete Markless grammar/corpus.
Multi-file/default-thread lint, config/ignore/reporters, JS plugins, type-aware rules, native formatting, Vite+, editor, packaging, and final Markless acceptance remain required.
Rejected JS/Prettier and Zig/Yuku controls are still present only because T011 forbade deletion until Rust equivalence passed; they should now be removed in the next Worker package.
